safeDefault.reason: No backend has independent review plus real three-OS product evidence.

directions.name: Container runtime cục bộ do AI for Boss quản lý

isolation.basis: OpenClaw Docker uses container namespaces and defaults to no network, read-only root and all capabilities dropped; Docker still shares a host or VM kernel and the daemon is a privileged attack surface unless rootless.

installationAndPrivilege: A container engine or desktop VM backend must exist and remain healthy.
Windows per-user Docker Desktop can install without admin, but WSL 2 or another supported VM backend and hardware virtualization remain prerequisites.
macOS can avoid selected privileged helpers, but default setup requests limited privileged configuration.
Linux rootless Docker reduces daemon privilege but requires subordinate UID/GID prerequisites.

dataAndNetwork.workspace: Local bind or isolated copy; any bind expands host exposure.
dataAndNetwork.externalDataTransfer: No sandbox data leaves the device unless a separately approved provider or network route is enabled.
lockedControls: No host Docker socket inside an agent container
No host network or container namespace join
No external bind outside approved project roots
No secret in container environment metadata

costLicenseDependency.software: Locked OpenClaw source is MIT. Docker Engine/Moby open-source licensing differs from Docker Desktop subscription terms.
costLicenseDependency.commercial: Docker Desktop requires a paid subscription for larger enterprises under Docker terms; redistribution and embedding require legal review.
costLicenseDependency.externalDependency: Container engine, image supply chain and OS virtualization stack.

recoveryUpdateFailure.failure: Missing daemon, image or platform prerequisite must fail closed without host-exec fallback.
recoveryUpdateFailure.recovery: Recreate the sandbox from verified config and image; keep user-owned workspace canonical only through an explicit grant.
recoveryUpdateFailure.update: Pin image/runtime compatibility, stage updates and retain a rollback path.

directions.name: Sandbox từ xa qua OpenShell hoặc SSH

isolation.basis: OpenClaw moves tool execution to an SSH-accessible host or OpenShell-managed environment. NVIDIA labels OpenShell alpha software; AI for Boss therefore does not accept it as a production default without later maturity, security and operations evidence.

installationAndPrivilege: Requires OpenSSH client plus host identity material for generic SSH.
OpenShell requires plugin, CLI, account or gateway access and sandbox policy.
Remote compute, lifecycle and policy are outside the local desktop trust boundary.

dataAndNetwork.workspace: SSH seeds a remote-canonical workspace; OpenShell mirror uploads and downloads every exec turn while remote mode seeds once and keeps remote state canonical.
dataAndNetwork.externalDataTransfer: Selected workspace content, tool input/output and metadata cross the network to the remote environment.
lockedControls: No silent mirror or remote-mode switch
No production OpenShell while upstream labels it alpha
No sensitive browser because locked backends do not support it

costLicenseDependency.software: OpenShell is Apache-2.0 and the locked OpenClaw plugin is under the OpenClaw MIT repository.
costLicenseDependency.commercial: Remote compute, storage, egress, support and account pricing are operator/provider costs; no product cost model is proven.
costLicenseDependency.externalDependency: Network, remote host identity, account, policy service and remote lifecycle.

recoveryUpdateFailure.failure: Network, SSH identity, host-key or remote lifecycle failure must stop the task and preserve local state.
recoveryUpdateFailure.recovery: SSH/OpenShell recreate can delete remote canonical state and reseed; recovery requires explicit user-visible state ownership.
recoveryUpdateFailure.update: Client, plugin, remote gateway, image and policy versions must remain compatible.

directions.name: Cơ chế hạn chế native theo từng hệ điều hành

isolation.basis: Windows AppContainer, macOS App Sandbox and Linux namespaces/seccomp/Landlock/cgroup expose different contracts. Linux seccomp documentation explicitly says syscall filtering alone is not a sandbox.

installationAndPrivilege: Windows AppContainer needs a dedicated launcher, capability and ACL design; Windows Sandbox excludes Home and is an optional VM feature.
macOS App Sandbox requires entitlements and signed helper design; arbitrary toolchains need explicit helper packaging and inheritance.
Linux needs a maintained composition of namespaces, seccomp, Landlock and cgroup with kernel and distribution compatibility handling.

dataAndNetwork.workspace: Must be implemented separately for each OS and cannot reuse one cross-platform OpenClaw backend contract.
dataAndNetwork.externalDataTransfer: Native controls do not define provider or application data egress by themselves.
lockedControls: No App Sandbox claim for unsigned arbitrary child tools
No Windows Sandbox automation as a product backend without lifecycle evidence

costLicenseDependency.software: OS APIs have no separate runtime subscription, but implementation, signing and maintenance costs are high.
costLicenseDependency.commercial: Windows edition constraints and Apple Developer signing/distribution requirements remain.
costLicenseDependency.externalDependency: OS version, kernel features, code signing, entitlements and platform-specific security expertise.

recoveryUpdateFailure.failure: Any unsupported primitive or launcher failure must deny execution, which creates many platform-specific failure branches.
recoveryUpdateFailure.recovery: Requires separate process-tree cleanup, storage cleanup and policy migration per OS.
recoveryUpdateFailure.update: Every OS update can change available primitives, entitlements, kernel ABI or compatibility.

nextEvidenceRequired: Senior platform and independent security review
Product Owner selection of runtime ownership and commercial dependency
Real Docker-compatible sandbox tests on supported Windows macOS and Linux machines
Installer privilege and ordinary-user usability study
Crash update rollback and daemon-unavailable recovery tests
Network egress and filesystem escape adversarial tests

claims.statement: Locked OpenClaw Docker defaults are no network, read-only root, and all capabilities dropped.
Docker rootless mode runs daemon and containers without root privileges when prerequisites are met.
A hardened managed local container is the preferred contingent implementation direction.
sectionLocators: ADR Recommendation; local managed container analysis

claims.statement: OpenShell uses remote managed sandboxes and NVIDIA labels the reviewed software alpha.
sectionLocators: OpenClaw OpenShell backend; NVIDIA README alpha notice; Support Matrix

claims.statement: OpenShell and SSH remain explicit opt-in research only and cannot become the production default in Feature 0.6.
Windows, macOS, and Linux expose different isolation primitives, and seccomp filtering alone is not a sandbox.
Native OS restrictions are defense-in-depth and not one primary cross-platform agent backend.
A dedicated installer and recovery flow may make a managed local container usable for ordinary nontechnical users.
sectionLocators: Windows install prerequisites; Mac permission requirements
